domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Central aggregate for leave applications. Tracks full lifecycle from draft through approval/rejection/cancellation. Orchestrates policy validation, balance checks, and manager routing.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Holds employment status (ACTIVE, ON_LEAVE, INACTIVE, PROBATION) which gates leave eligibility. managerId defines the approval chain.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave balance per type per year. Enforces that requests do not exceed available balance. Updated atomically on approval (used += days, pending -= days) and on cancellation (reverse).

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines rules and constraints per leave type, optionally scoped by role/department. Used to validate requests and compute entitlements. Versioned via effective dates; only one ACTIVE policy per (type, role, department) at a time.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type has distinct policy rules and balance tracking. Stored as a reference table for extensibility but treated as a domain enum.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable record of all state-changing operations (GP-002). Captures who did what to which entity and the delta.

modules.name: leave-status
owns: LeaveStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Foundation — Enums, Audit, and Employee
recommended_phases.rationale: Leaf modules with zero internal dependencies. leave-type and leave-status are pure enums. audit-log is the cross-cutting audit service required by GP-002. employee provides identity and manager hierarchy needed by all downstream modules. These must exist before anything else.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Policy and Notification
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-policy depends only on leave-type and audit-log (both in Phase 1). notification depends only on employee (Phase 1). These are independent of each other and can be built in parallel, but both are prerequisites for leave-balance and leave-request.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Leave Balance
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-balance depends on leave-policy (Phase 2), employee (Phase 1), and audit-log (Phase 1). It provides the balance tracking, deduction, and restoration that leave-request needs for validation and lifecycle management.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Leave Request — Core Application Logic
recommended_phases.rationale: leave-request is the orchestrating module that depends on every other module. It wires together policy validation, balance checks, manager approval routing, audit recording, and notification dispatch. Building it last ensures all dependencies are stable.

architecture_md_update:
## Leave Management Module

### Domain Entities

- **LeaveRequest** — Central aggregate for leave applications. Lifecycle: `DRAFT → SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED` (terminal unless cancelled), `→ REJECTED` (terminal), `→ CANCELLED` (terminal from SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, or APPROVED).
- **Employee** — Organisation member with status `ACTIVE`, `ON_LEAVE`, `INACTIVE`, `PROBATION`. `managerId` defines the approval chain.
- **LeaveBalance** — Per-employee, per-type, per-year balance. Tracks `entitled`, `used`, `pending`, `carriedOver`, `remaining`. Status: `ACTIVE`, `EXHAUSTED`, `FROZEN`.
- **LeavePolicy** — Rules per leave type, optionally scoped by role/department. Versioned via `effectiveFrom`/`effectiveTo`. Status: `ACTIVE`, `SUPERSEDED`, `DEPRECATED`.
- **LeaveType** — Enumeration (`ANNUAL`, `SICK`, `EMERGENCY`). Stored as a reference table for extensibility.
- **AuditLog** — Immutable record of all state changes (GP-002).

### Conceptual Data Model (PostgreSQL)

| Table | Key Fields | Notes |
|-------|------------|-------|
| `employee` | id, user_id, email, role, manager_id, department, status | RBAC via role; manager hierarchy for approvals |
| `leave_type` | id, code, label, is_active | Reference data for leave categories |
| `leave_policy` | id, leave_type_id, role, department, entitlement_per_year, max_consecutive_days, min_notice_hours, requires_approval, requires_documentation, probation_eligible, allow_carry_over, carry_over_cap, effective_from, effective_to, status | Scoped policies; only one ACTIVE per (type, role, dept) at a time |
| `leave_balance` | id, employee_id, leave_type_id, leave_policy_id, year, entitled, used, pending, carried_over, remaining, status | Unique per (employee, type, year); updated atomically on approval/cancellation |
| `leave_request` | id, employee_id, leave_type_id, leave_policy_id, status, start_date, end_date, total_days, manager_id, reviewed_by, submitted_at, reviewed_at | Overlap detection via date-range indexes; manager_id for routing |
| `audit_log` | id, entity_type, entity_id, action, actor_id, changes, created_at | Immutable; supports GP-002 |

### Module Structure (Fastify + TypeScript)

```
src/modules/
  leave-type/          # Enum + reference model
  leave-status/        # Status enum + transition rules
  employee/            # Employee model, repo, service
  audit-log/           # Audit model, repo, service (cross-cutting)
  leave-policy/        # Policy model, repo, service
  leave-balance/       # Balance model, repo, service
  notification/        # Notification model, repo, service
  leave-request/       # Orchestrator: model, repo, service, controller, routes, DTOs
```

### Dependency Map (acyclic)

```
leave-request ──→ leave-balance ──→ leave-policy ──→ leave-type
    │                 │                  │
    │                 │                  └──→ audit-log
    │                 │
    │                 └──→ employee ──→ audit-log
    │
    ├──→ leave-status (leaf)
    ├──→ notification ──→ employee
    └──→ audit-log (leaf)
```

### Business Rules Summary

- **BR-001** Submission: employee ACTIVE, policy ACTIVE, notice period met (except EMERGENCY), max consecutive days not exceeded, sufficient balance, no overlapping approved leave. Moves `DRAFT → SUBMITTED`, increments `pending`.
- **BR-002** Approval/Rejection: only designated manager. Approval: `SUBMITTED/UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED`, `used += days`, `pending -= days`. Rejection: `→ REJECTED`, `pending -= days`.
- **BR-003** Cancellation: employee cancels own request if SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, or APPROVED. Restores balance if previously approved.
- **BR-004** Balance initialisation: new year creates balance from policy entitlement + carry-over (capped).
- **BR-005** Overlap prevention: checked at submission and approval.
- **BR-006** Emergency leave bypasses `minNoticeHours`.
- **BR-007** Sick leave may require documentation; manager can move to UNDER_REVIEW while waiting.
- **BR-008** Probation employees only eligible for leave types with `probationEligible = true`.

### Golden Principles Compliance

- **GP-001 (Repository pattern)**: All state changes go through repository interfaces with concrete `Pg*` implementations backed by PostgreSQL via `pg` Pool.
- **GP-002 (Audit trail)**: Every create/update/status transition on leave_request, leave_balance, leave_policy, and employee writes an immutable `audit_log` record.
- **GP-005 (RBAC)**: Employee `role` field enforces access control; controller layer checks that the caller is the employee (submit/cancel) or the designated manager (approve/reject).

### Lifecycle States (all domain-introduced states reflected)

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, UNDER_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED
- **Employee**: ACTIVE, ON_LEAVE, INACTIVE, PROBATION
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, DEPRECATED
- **LeaveType**: (static, no lifecycle)
- **AuditLog**: (immutable, no lifecycle)

### Implementation Phases

1. **Foundation**: `leave-type`, `leave-status`, `audit-log`, `employee`
2. **Policy & Notification**: `leave-policy`, `notification`
3. **Balance**: `leave-balance`
4. **Core**: `leave-request` (orchestrator)

All modules use Fastify for HTTP, Jest for testing, and follow the modular-monolith structure with clear service boundaries.
sql_schemas: table employee | fields: id, user_id, first_name, last_name, email, role, manager_id, department, designation, date_of_joining, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employee.id | indexes: email: unique lookup for authentication and identity; role: RBAC enforcement queries filter by role (GP-005); manager_id: direct-report lookups for manager approval workflows; department: departmental leave reports and aggregate queries

table leave_type | fields: id, code, label, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: code: unique lookup by leave type code; is_active: filtering active leave types for dropdowns and policy lookups

table leave_policy | fields: id, leave_type_id, role, department, entitlement_per_year, max_consecutive_days, min_notice_hours, requires_approval, requires_documentation, probation_eligible, allow_carry_over, carry_over_cap, effective_from, effective_to, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_type.id | indexes: leave_type_id: policy lookup by leave type; role: role-scoped policy queries; department: department-scoped policy queries; status: filtering active policies

table leave_balance | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, leave_policy_id, year, entitled, used, pending, carried_over, remaining, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employee.id; leave_type_id -> leave_type.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policy.id | indexes: employee_id: per-employee balance lookups; leave_type_id: balance queries by leave type; year: annual balance scoping; employee_id, leave_type_id, year: unique composite lookup for current balance

table leave_request | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, leave_policy_id, status, start_date, end_date, total_days, reason, manager_id, manager_comment, reviewed_by, submitted_at, reviewed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employee.id; leave_type_id -> leave_type.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policy.id; manager_id -> employee.id; reviewed_by -> employee.id | indexes: employee_id: employee views own leave history; status: filtering pending requests for manager approval queues; manager_id: manager views requests they must approve; reviewed_by: manager views requests they have reviewed; leave_type_id: filtering by leave type; start_date, end_date: overlap detection when validating new requests; employee_id, status: common composite query for 'my pending requests'; created_at: chronological listing of requests

table audit_log | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, actor_id, changes, created_at | pk: id | fks: actor_id -> employee.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookup audit trail for a specific entity; actor_id: audit trail by user; action: filtering by action type; created_at: chronological audit log queries
